newsitem.title: FRANCE: Strauss-Kahn sees French growth up at 3-pct end-97.
newsitem.headline: Strauss-Kahn sees French growth up at 3-pct end-97.

text.p: French Finance Minister Dominique Strauss-Kahn said on Thursday his analysis of the current economic situation allowed him to believe that France could reach a growth rate of three percent by the end of the year.
Strauss-Kahn told a news conference his analysis allowed him to expect "an upturn (in growth) by the end of the year," when it could reach a "rate of three percent".
Strauss-Kahn said his view was based on expectations of an increase in consumption on top of export-led growth.
Strauss-Kahn said he expected the additional growth to come from a boost in spending power of around one percent, compared with a traditional increase of about 0.5 percent in spending power per year.
Asked about the impact this would have on the deficit, Strauss-Kahn said that increases in growth only had a gradual impact.
"It happens progressively. This will not happen between now and the end the year," he said.
